# Switch

Switch models a persistent checked or pressed state with explicit ownership.

## Basic usage

Switch starts off so its immediate toggle behavior is clear.

<ComponentExample component="switch" scenario="off" title="Switch" description="Switch starts off so its immediate toggle behavior is clear." :index="0" />

## Features

- Binary value.
- Toggle.
- Idempotent set.

Each feature is part of the public semantic contract. Host packages may expose different input and rendering helpers while preserving accepted transitions.



## Example cases

### On

Switch starts on and exposes the active state without changing its label.

<ComponentExample component="switch" scenario="on" title="On" description="Switch starts on and exposes the active state without changing its label." :index="1" />

### Controlled

The parent owns the current value and applies every accepted change back to Switch.

## State ownership

State that changes application-owned data supports controlled or uncontrolled ownership where the component contract permits it. Use uncontrolled state for local behavior and controlled state when a parent coordinates validation, persistence, or multiple controls.

## Disabled and readonly

Host projections distinguish disabled interaction from readonly inspection when the underlying control permits both. Disabled controls leave the interaction sequence; readonly controls remain available for inspection while rejecting mutation.

## Semantics

The component contract follows [the relevant accessibility pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/). Visual styling remains outside the package; use host attributes, parts, and state projections as styling hooks.
